name: Gang of Four
label: EMI
lede: Four Leeds students took their name from a Chinese political purge, walked off Top of the Pops rather than change one word, and played a guitar so brittle and funky that Flea, Kurt Cobain and Michael Stipe all pointed to it as an influence.

eras.title: A name from the newsstand
eras.text: Gang of Four started in Leeds in 1976 among university students steeped in Marxist theory, Situationism and dub reggae. Their first single, on a tiny Edinburgh label, topped the indie chart and became a favorite of the BBC's John Peel.

years.h: Dave Wolfson plays two gigs, then Dave Allen takes his bass
years.p: Singer [[Jon King|e2472ddb-f53f-4853-b839-2ed07e2d4064]], guitarist [[Andy Gill|eb3f978d-272a-460d-bc3e-a1a82ecb8147]] and drummer [[Hugo Burnham|9c965e30-7658-4658-b5f2-08fff1874bd2]] start the band in Leeds with Wolfson on bass. [[Dave Allen|829dc2aa-99d2-44ad-ad1e-76533b14d512]] replaces him after two gigs.

years.h: A newspaper billboard about a Maoist purge becomes the band's name
years.p: Driving with Gill and King, Andy Corrigan of [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]] spots a billboard about China's Gang of Four, the purged Maoist faction, and suggests it.

years.h: Damaged Goods goes to No. 1 on the indie chart
years.p: Edinburgh's Fast Product puts out the EP with (Love Like) Anthrax and Armalite Rifle. John Peel plays it and brings the band in for two sessions.
years.xp: Rolling Stone later put Damaged Goods on its 2020 list of the 100 greatest debut singles. It was the band's first single.

eras.title: Entertainment!, then a walkout
eras.text: EMI signed them, and the debut they made put King's lyrics about commodities, work, sex and the Troubles over Gill's jagged, stop-start guitar and a rhythm section that played like a funk band. Then they walked off the biggest music show on British TV.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gang of Four · Wikipedia: Entertainment!
yt: At Home He's a Tourist, the promo video
years.h: The BBC wants one word changed, so Gang of Four leave Top of the Pops
years.p: Booked to play At Home He's a Tourist, the band is told to swap a word about condoms for a cleaner one. They refuse and walk off.
years.xp:
The BBC then banned the single from its radio and TV, and EMI's enthusiasm cooled. The song still reached No. 58 on the UK singles chart, the band's highest placing.

Wikipedia gives the swap the BBC wanted as one word for another, rubbers to rubbish, and dates none of it beyond 1979.

q: Gang of Four could really swing. I stole a lot from them.
years.src: Wikipedia: Entertainment! · Wikipedia: Gang of Four
years.h: Entertainment! lands on EMI with a cowboy shaking hands on the sleeve
years.p: Recorded at the Workhouse on London's Old Kent Road and produced by Gill, King and manager Rob Warr. Warner Bros. puts it out in America.
years.xp:
King designed the cover: a cowboy and an Indian shaking hands in three processed versions, with a caption that reads "The Indian smiles, he thinks that the cowboy is his friend. The cowboy smiles, he is glad the Indian is fooled."

Rolling Stone's David Fricke called it the best debut album by a British band since the Clash's first. [[Kurt Cobain|3c9b356d-d1db-4f4e-a7a3-2d00c1d70255]] put it 13th on his list of 50 favorite albums, and [[Flea|2dc7a305-7a8c-4fcc-add4-5e9def0a9a0d]] said it completely changed the way he looked at rock music. It had sold over 100,000 copies in the UK by 2009.

eras.title: Three bassists and one banned single
eras.text: The original four came apart one member at a time. Allen left, a Parliament and Talking Heads sideman filled in, and Sara Lee brought a smoother bottom end just as the Falklands War got I Love a Man in a Uniform pulled from the radio. By 1983 it was over.

years.big: Probably the best politically motivated band in rock & roll
yt: He'd Send in the Army, live 1980
years.h: Solid Gold turns spare and analytical
years.p: That's Rolling Stone's David Fricke, on the band. The EMI follow-up has Cheeseburger, He'd Send in the Army and In the Ditch.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls the record uncompromising and spare, with King's lyrics working through the paradoxes of warfare, work and leisure. It was Dave Allen's last album with the band.

years.h: Dave Allen quits, and Shriekback is born
years.p: Allen starts [[Shriekback|748161b8-ec62-4423-b6f1-3a8026190ebb]] with ex-[[XTC|97c86b2c-2765-46a2-aef8-76a7e24c430f]] keyboardist Barry Andrews. Busta "Cherry" Jones, who has played with [[Parliament|d1947987-9614-49ae-bd36-8000e6b6f7d0]] and [[Talking Heads|a94a7155-c79d-4409-9fcf-220cb0e4dc3a]], fills in until Sara Lee of Robert Fripp's League of Gentlemen joins.
years.xp: Allen stayed with Shriekback until 1988, then founded King Swamp and the label World Domination Recordings. Years later he worked at Intel and, after Apple bought Beats Music in 2014, at Apple Music.

years.cap: Gang of Four in a 1982 promo portrait
years.h: The BBC pulls I Love a Man in a Uniform in the middle of the Falklands War
years.p: The single from Songs of the Free looked like the band's radio breakthrough until the BBC dropped it from airplay in 1982.
play: I Love a Man in a Uniform

years.h: Hugo Burnham leaves to start Illustrated Man
years.p: The drummer quits in spring 1983, after Songs of the Free. He later drums for PiL and ABC, manages [[Shriekback|748161b8-ec62-4423-b6f1-3a8026190ebb]], and becomes an A&R man in New York.
years.xp: Burnham managed Shriekback with his old bandmate Allen from 1985 to 1988, then moved to New York and worked in A&R at Island, Imago, Qwest and EMI Music Publishing.

years.h: One more album, Hard, and Gang of Four is done
years.p: King, Gill and Sara Lee make it as a trio for EMI. The band breaks up afterward.

eras.title: Gill and King, twice more
eras.text: Gill and King brought the name back as a duo with hired players for two Polydor albums. Neither made much noise, but the name kept its pull.

years.h: Mall brings Gang of Four back on Polydor
years.p: Gill and King are joined on bass by [[Gail Ann Dorsey|3363921c-9099-40af-93cc-1b15d0e46fc5]], who later plays with David Bowie.

years.h: After Shrinkwrapped, nothing until 2004
years.p: It's the second Polydor album from Gill and King. Gang of Four then go quiet until the original line-up gets back together.

eras.title: The original four, then just two
eras.text: With Franz Ferdinand, Bloc Party and The Rapture all sounding a lot like them, the original line-up got back on stage for the first time since 1981. Burnham and Allen were gone again within two years; Gill and King kept going until 2012.

years.big: I knew we could do it, when I saw we all still had our hair
years.src: Wikipedia: Hugo Burnham · Wikipedia: Gang of Four
yt: Gill and King on post-punk history, 2009
years.h: The original four reunite, first time since 1981
years.p: Burnham, to the New York Times, on getting back with King, Gill and Allen. They announce it in November 2004, tour the UK in January 2005, then play the US twice that year.
years.xp: The reunion also took in European and Japanese dates. Burnham was blunt about the plan: "What resonates is the old stuff."

years.h: Return the Gift puts the old songs back through the studio
years.p: Gang of Four re-record songs from Entertainment!, Solid Gold and Songs of the Free, and add remixes.

years.h: Burnham and Allen leave again, and the original four are done
years.p: Mark Heaney takes over drums from Burnham, who is teaching at the New England Institute of Art in Boston. Allen also leaves; by Content the bassist is Thomas McNeice.
years.xp: Burnham's last show with the reunion line-up was at All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead, England, in December 2006.

years.cap: Jon King and Andy Gill at the Metro, Chicago, February 11, 2011
years.h: Content, the last album with King, gets four stars from the New York Times
years.p: Gill produces it at his London studio. Jon Pareles says the band has reclaimed its old attack.
years.xp: Gill and engineer Sam Morton recorded it in 2009 and 2010 at Gill's Beauchamp Building studio in central London. It came out on Grönland in Europe and Yep Roc in the US, and Eddi Reader sings backing vocals. Metacritic puts it at 71 out of 100.

years.h: Gill keeps Gang of Four, with John Sterry on vocals, against King's wishes
years.p: After the Content tours, King and Gill disagree about the band's direction and stop working together.

eras.title: Andy Gill's Gang of Four
eras.text: For eight years Gang of Four was Gill and a younger band, making records with guests from The Kills to the German rock star Herbert Grönemeyer. It ended when Gill died at 64, weeks after a tour of China.

years.h: Sterry takes over vocals on What Happens Next
years.p: Guests include [[Alison Mosshart|054f94f3-2a75-480b-b417-d817cdbcf6f6]] of the Kills, [[Herbert Grönemeyer|456eabce-d1dd-4481-a206-36ab4f2eaeb8]] and guitarist Tomoyasu Hotei. Gill is the only original member left.

years.h: Gill releases Happy Now himself, the last album he completes
years.p: Self-released on his own label in April, seven months before the tour of China.

years.h: Gang of Four tour China in November 2019
years.p: Gill takes the band there. He dies within three months.

years.cap: Gang of Four at the Rockaway Beach festival
years.h: Andy Gill dies in London at 64
years.p: He dies on February 1, 2020. The first reports said pneumonia and multiple organ failure; his widow, the journalist Catherine Mayer, concluded in May that he was an early COVID-19 victim after the China tour.
years.xp:
Critics described Gill's rhythm guitar as "metal splintering": a cold Stratocaster through transistor amps, all treble attack.

He also produced the [[Red Hot Chili Peppers|8bfac288-ccc5-448d-9573-c33ea2aa5c30]]' 1984 debut, [[The Jesus Lizard|dfebd6c0-dae7-4cc8-a8e9-0dbaa382209f]]'s Blue, [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]] and [[The Futureheads|0cf9d983-aecf-4d57-9e94-fde2beac014f]]. Mayer co-founded Britain's Women's Equality Party. Two EPs of his last recordings, This Heaven Gives Me Migraine and Anti Hero, came out after his death.

eras.title: The Long Goodbye
eras.text: A tribute album and a box set sent listeners back to the classic records, and King and Burnham took the band back out, first with David Pajo of Slint on guitar, then Ted Leo. They called the last tour the Long Goodbye, then kept finding reasons to play.

years.h: Other artists cover the band on The Problem of Leisure
years.p: The full title is The Problem of Leisure: A Celebration of Andy Gill and Gang of Four, a tribute album made after Gill's death.

years.cap: Gang of Four at the Black Cat, Washington DC
years.h: David Pajo of Slint takes Gill's place for the reunion
years.p: King, Burnham and Sara Lee of the early-1980s line-up return, with [[David Pajo|85188c46-d3ed-4517-ba78-5d06ec764f1c]] on guitar.
years.xp: The four set out on US touring for 2022.

years.h: King's art direction on the 77-81 box earns a Grammy nomination
years.p: The Gang of Four 77-81 box collects the classic-era records. The 2022 nomination comes as the band tours the US behind it.

years.h: Gang of Four announce a last headlining tour of the US and Europe
years.p: King and Burnham are joined by [[Ted Leo|3b7051df-c423-4d90-a6ca-aa10c363445d]] on guitar and [[Gail Greenwood|d86b84e3-6c11-4499-a453-82e8744bc08e]] on bass. King's memoir To Hell With Poverty! also comes out in 2025.

years.h: Founding bassist Dave Allen dies at 69
years.p: Burnham told Stereogum that Allen had been living with early-onset dementia for several years.

years.h: Wilco's Solid Sound Festival books Gang of Four after all
years.p: At MASS MoCA, [[Wilco|9e53f84d-ef44-4c16-9677-5fd4d78cbd7d]]'s festival lists them, and the band explains that the Long Goodbye was only their last headline tour.

years.h: A new single, No Kings Here!, written for the protests
years.p: Nick Launay, who worked on 1981's Another Day/Another Dollar, produces it for the No Kings protests across North America. King is on a new Gang of Four song for the first time in 15 years.
years.xp: It's also Burnham's first new Gang of Four recording in about 44 years, the first with Leo and Greenwood, and the first Gang of Four song made without Gill.
